newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM sees sale well underway next year.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM sees sale well underway next year.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) said on Friday privatisation of the company could be well underway during the second half of next year.
ZCCM technical director John Patterson told Reuters that analysis of bids from the 39 companies which pre-qualified to buy ZCCM's mining and power assets would begin around March 1997.

"Hopefully with the bids coming in at the end of February, and by the time we get to the middle of the calendar year, we would hope to see some of the packages at a pretty advanced stage," Patterson said in an interview.
He said the sale of some of the larger packages, including the Nchanga, Nkana and Luanshya divisions, could take more time to be settled.
"Some of the packages because they are large packages, may take a little bit longer," he said.
The Zambia Privatisation Agency has offered the assets of ZCCM -- the country's largest public enterprise -- for sale in nine packages.
Patterson said ZCCM did not favour any individual company from the 39 pre-qualifiers, six of them bidding only for the power generation and distribution assets.
"We have a number of very well-known names in the mining world included in our list.

"I guess the only criteria really... is to encourage a reasonable level of diversification of new owners, so we have the opportunity in the country for input into the industry both financially from a number of different parts of the world and technologically as well," Patterson said.
"Other than that there is no real preference to a particular company."
Among the companies which pre-qualified are Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, which already holds a minority stake, Anglovaal Ltd and Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd (BHP).
Patterson said ZCCM was holding back on new investment in view of the planned privatisation.
"We have restrained ourselves this financial year and I'm sure we will next financial year, in terms of the level of reinvestment in the company," he said.

"Obviously the new owners, one of the things that they are expected to bring to the party at the end of the day is new investment. They will themselves select their priorities for investment," Patterson said.
The ZPA has said at least $2 billion worth of new investment was needed on the Copperbelt to bring the mines up to modern standards.
